scope: UART 8N1 RX core only: independent RTL/TB/scripts, existing lawful Icarus 12/vvp, bounded N=8/16/234 simulations. No FIFO, parity, flow control, address map, bus wrapper, CPU/SoC, REGIF, board clock/PLL or hardware test.

tools.legal_source: Existing lawful local Icarus installation recorded in B-ENV; explicit path passed, PATH unchanged.

design.frame: 8N1: 1 start low, 8 data LSB-first, 1 stop high, idle high, no parity/FIFO/flow control/BREAK detection.
design.clks_per_bit: integer N >= 8, default 16; N<8 explicitly rejected at simulation start.
design.synchronizer: exactly two async-reset-to-1 FFs; main logic reads only pre-edge second stage; d=E2.
design.sampling: start d+floor(N/2); data d+N+floor(N/2)+k*N; stop S=d+9N+floor(N/2).
design.publish: good stop publishes rx_data/rx_valid in S NBA; no extra S+1 pipeline delay.
design.back_to_back: raw bit period N*T; raw frame period 10*N*T; same-phase d_next=d+10N, no +1 and no inserted idle.
design.mailbox: one-byte level valid; full+not-ready keeps old and sets overrun; full+ready consumes old and replaces new with valid held; bad stop never writes data.
design.errors: frame_error and overrun are independent sticky flags; clear_errors clears a bit only when no new event of that bit occurs on the same edge.
design.reset: async low assertion clears mailbox/errors/state; two warmup edges then arm only after pre-edge second stage is high; low after reset is ignored until a real high then falling edge.

configurations.purpose: short-frame and four-phase boundary coverage plus same-byte replacement
default configuration; four phases, back-to-back frames, false start, same-byte replacement

expected_per_configuration.tb_hard_cap_enforced: Runner rejects plan cycle budgets >1000000; TB emits TB_HARD_CAP_REJECT if TB_MAX_CYCLES >1000000.
expected_per_configuration.job_budget_rule: Each configuration freezes last_check_cycle and uses tb_max_cycles = last_check_cycle + 32; runner/TB reject >1000000.
expected_per_configuration.process_timeout_classification: FAIL for the deliberate watchdog; only TB_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT with native rc=0 is TIMEOUT mechanism success.
expected_per_configuration.budget_authority: Per configs[].tb_max_cycles; no 106285 or 200000 legacy budget is active.

cases.purpose: valid frames and LSB-first byte order
cases.expected: For each of 0x00,0xFF,0x55,0xAA,0x01,0x80,0x7E: valid/data appear at S_postNBA; no frame_error/overrun; after consume valid=0 and data holds.

cases.purpose: four sampling phases and representative frames
cases.expected: N8/N16: 0.1/0.3/0.6/0.9T phases for 0x55 and 0xAA; N234: 0x55 and 0xAA representative frames; all valid/data at S_postNBA, no errors.

cases.purpose: true back-to-back frames with no extra idle
cases.expected: N16 16 frames, N8 8 frames, N234 2 frames; raw frame period exactly 10*N*T; same-phase d_next=d+10N; each S_postNBA shows the expected byte, S+1 consumes it, no overrun/frame_error.
Low durations L=7 and L=8 (pre-second-stage samples) with return high before start center are ignored; no valid/error; a following good 0x5A is accepted.

cases.purpose: bad stop, mailbox hold/consume, sustained low, clear/new-error priority
cases.expected: Bad stop sets frame_error, writes no data; ready=0 keeps old, ready=1 consumes old; sustained low does not create a second visible frame; full mailbox recovery sets overrun; clear with new frame_error keeps new FE and clears old OV. 5e: clear_errors with a new overrun keeps the new OV=1, clears the old FE, and leaves the full mailbox byte 0x11 held. The new good frame 0x44 is still a protocol DROP (OV already 1, no OV rise; independent serial-decoded data). 5f: bad stop with a sustained low tail clears FE while low, confirms no re-raise during the low tail, and recovers after high.
Good byte appears at S_postNBA; valid&&!ready holds 24+ cycles; one ready handshake consumes exactly once; data holds after consume.

cases.purpose: full mailbox, overrun, clear, same-byte non-dedup
cases.expected: Second good byte with full mailbox keeps old, drops new, sets overrun; clear_errors clears overrun without consuming; after consume, the same byte value is accepted again.

cases.purpose: same-edge consume old plus replace new
cases.expected: With valid=1 and ready asserted only for S: old consumed, new data published at S, valid remains 1, no overrun; new byte is consumed at S+1 when ready stays high. The ledger records CONSUME old plus ACCEPT-REPLACE at the same edge with edge/time and pre/post public states; same-byte replacement is not rejected merely because rx_data does not change.

Mid-frame reset cancels in-flight frame and clears outputs; release-low stays ignored until high then falling; clear with a new frame_error keeps FE=1 and clears the other error where applicable. Mid-frame reset is exercised during DATA, START and STOP; CANCEL is derived from reset while the independent serial decoder reports an active frame, not by a post-stimulus actual_cancel() call. Each cancels the in-flight frame and a following good frame is accepted.

negative.note: Formal capture-path controls: same-edge, DROP, CANCEL; missing/extra/order/wrong-byte and missing/extra DROP/CANCEL; shared comparator macro on captured events. Status-propagation selfcheck is separate.
negative.capture_source: rx_public_capture is driven by public valid/ready/data/line_good/line_data/cancel inputs; it captures same-byte replacement, DROP and CANCEL streams and feeds the shared ordered comparator. The negatives are generated from captured event streams, not hand-filled actual arrays.

watchdog.note: A process timeout without TB_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT is FAIL, not mechanism success.

illegal_config.note: N<8 must be rejected at simulation start; no silent clamp.

limitations: Simulation-only: no PDS synthesis, place-and-route, timing analysis, JTAG, download, Flash, board loopback or temperature test was performed; hardware remains STOPPED.
Only public RX ports are observed; no claim is made about internal nodes or physical metastability/MTBF.
Icarus Verilog 12 logical-cycle simulation does not prove physical baud tolerance, noise immunity, CDC layout or board-level reliability.
N=234 is a representative divider calculation, not a board measurement or a claim that the CPU is running at 27 MHz.
The two-stage synchronizer proves logical latency only, not analog metastability or MTBF.
PASS_REHEARSAL, local PASS and this plan's PASS are not mainline reproduction, interface compatibility, system integration or hardware acceptance.
The 1.1.0 plan adds RX contract-boundary cases and runner mechanism evidence; it is not a TX/GPIO full-matrix rerun and not a hardware/system acceptance.

The 1.2.0 plan adds a frozen ordered transaction ledger, +32-cycle per-config budgets, shared comparator negative proof, and process-timeout/log-truncation rejection; it is not a new full-matrix claim.
The 1.3.0 ledger adds protocol-derived events, edge/time and public pre/post states. It does not claim observation of hidden physical write pulses or replace the aggregate public-state counters.
Only RX-05 5e adds one DROP per configuration; old 1.2.0 logs/counts are retained as history and are not rewritten.
1.3.1 changes only RX verification: same-byte replacement coverage, true pre/post clear state and capture-path DROP/CANCEL negatives. RX RTL is unchanged; 5e DROP data remains independently decoded.
1.3.2 changes only event timing/state capture and status propagation; RX RTL is unchanged.
1.3.3 only shares the RX public capture module and fixes one-based CONSUME/pre/post observation; RX RTL unchanged.
1.3.4 changes only RX capture/order/snapshot and status controls; RX RTL unchanged.
1.3.5 fixes only RX snapshot edge/time and plan/index consistency; RX RTL and functional expectations are unchanged. Counts remain 92/110/68 and 41/41, 50/50, 29/29.

event_ledger.purpose: Pre-freeze ordered accept/consume/drop/cancel expectations; TB increments expected counters as directed cases execute and asserts aggregate counts.
event_ledger.cancellation: Mid-frame DATA/START/STOP resets are checked by no stale valid/error and a following good frame; cancellation has no public count port.
event_ledger.authority: These counters are the single active values; functional_expected repeats them. Old 1.3.4 40/39,49/48,28/27 values are historical and not active.

ledger.delta_reason: RX-08 adds same-byte A1/A1 same-edge consume/replace: per configuration +1 ACCEPT (fill), +1 CONSUME +1 ACCEPT-REPLACE +1 CONSUME (same-edge sequence), for +4 events. The 5e DROP and its independent serial-decoded data remain unchanged.
ledger.drop_data_source: Independent raw-serial decoder on the external rx pin; not stim_bytes[0] and not a hidden physical write pulse.
ledger.drop_rule: A good serial frame completion (decoded start/data/stop) with pre-edge rx_valid=1 and rx_ready=0 is DROP. It is still DROP when OV was already 1 and clear_errors is asserted at the same S edge.
ledger.same_edge_rule: With valid=1 and ready=1 at the publish edge, the old byte is CONSUME and the new byte is ACCEPT-REPLACE even when the byte value is unchanged; ACCEPT is not inferred only from a valid rise.
ledger.accept_consume_rule: ACCEPT/CONSUME are ordered protocol events tied to the good-frame completion and public valid/ready; aggregate valid/consume/FE/OV counters remain separate observable-state checks.
ledger.cancel_rule: CANCEL is derived at reset assertion while the independent serial decoder reports an active frame. The old post-stimulus actual_cancel() call is removed; expected cancels remain in the frozen test sequence.
ledger.observable_state_limit: The TB does not claim to observe any hidden internal write pulse; pre/post states are public ports only.

pre_clear_5e.note: 5e pre and post clear_errors are both real public samples at edge 8081 (+1 ps after NBA); no pre-copy special case.

ledger.cancel_post_state: CANCEL pre/post fields are sampled from public ports after asynchronous reset settles; they are not a fixed zero literal. The current three reset cases legitimately settle to 0.

event_timebase.definition: Contract d/S edges; public edge is one-based. Pre state is the last settled pre-edge public state; post state is sampled after NBA. The drop event edge 8081 keeps its actual edge; CONSUME is recorded on its actual following one-based edge.
event_timebase.pre_post: pre at the true event edge before NBA; post at +1 ps after the same NBA, before 1 ns stimulus changes.
event_timebase.cancel: CANCEL post fields sampled from public ports after asynchronous reset; not fixed literals.

ledger.shared_capture: Formal TB instantiates rx_public_capture and compares each event type/data/edge one-to-one in order; negative TB instantiates the same module. No content-only equivalence.
ledger.shared_capture_rule: Formal and negative instantiate the same rx_public_capture; formal compares each event type/data/edge ordered one-to-one, not a multiset.
ledger.snapshot_rule: pre at the true event edge before NBA; post at +1 ps after the same NBA; DROP post_clear is the real sampled value, not copied from pre_clear.

functional_expected.note: Single authoritative values; matches event_ledger.expected_by_config and new run.

status_propagation.rule: nonzero native rc, truncated log, or global RX_SELFCHECK_FAIL forces FAIL in every case and in the runner exit; a per-case TEST_PASS cannot override.
status_propagation.verification: Run rx_status_selfcheck.py after the final RX run; require all_pass=true. Old 20261024-232527 run is historical, not an active reference.

R1_acceptance.rule: Every accepted ledger event has immutable pre values at the true S/consume edge and real post values at +1 ps after the same NBA; no X/Z, no missing/duplicate events, counts 92/110/68, functional 41/41, 50/50, 29/29.
R1_acceptance.mutation: Any stale/next-edge pre or post snapshot, X/Z, missing/duplicate event, or pre-copied DROP post_clear is rejected.
